finding.claim: Caller-supplied X-Session-User-Verified header is trusted as the authenticated identity, so any client can impersonate a user holding delete or write grants and bypass ACL checks on file delete and rename.
finding.source: HTTP request header X-Session-User-Verified (views.py:11), unvalidated and unsigned.
finding.sink: ensure_allowed(g.user, f, 'delete') then del STORE[fid] (views.py:17-18); is_allowed(g.user, f, 'write') then f['name'] assignment (views.py:25-27).

trace.note: before_request load_user registered for all routes
is_allowed returns action in resource['grants'].get(user, []) keyed on header value
on success the file is deleted

finding.guards_checked: No authentication gate in before_request or routes; no token/signature/session binding of the header; acl.py performs no identity validation; no gateway or proxy config in repo to strip or set the header; missing header yields None and grants.get(None) denies, so unauthenticated access is not separately exploitable. Exploitability is conditional on the service being reachable without a trusted gateway that sets or strips this header.

verdict.guard_found: none. views.py:9-11 (load_user) copies the X-Session-User-Verified header into g.user with no check. acl.py:4-5 (is_allowed) only does a dict lookup keyed on that value, and acl.py:8-10 (ensure_allowed) aborts on False, but nothing verifies the identity. views.py:17 and 25 are the only uses, and no gateway or header-stripping config exists in the repo.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code: views.py:11 takes the client-supplied header as the identity, and views.py:17-18 and 25-27 authorize and act on that value via acl.py:5, with no control in the repo that blocks it (the claim holds only if the service is reachable without a trusted proxy that sets or strips the header, which the repo cannot show either way).

finding.claim: Unhandled KeyError on unknown file IDs returns 500 while existing-but-unauthorized files return 403, creating an existence oracle for file IDs.
finding.sink: STORE[fid] lookup (views.py:16, 24) raising KeyError for missing IDs, versus 403 from acl.py:10 or views.py:26 for existing IDs.

trace.note: STORE[fid] raises KeyError for unknown ID, yielding 500
abort(403) for existing file lacking grant
same KeyError vs 403 split on rename route

finding.guards_checked: No existence normalization or uniform not-found response. Severity depends on how guessable file IDs are; ID generation is not in this repo so this could not be assessed.

verdict.guard_found: None effective. views.py:9-11 (before_request) only copies the X-Session-User-Verified header into g.user and enforces nothing. acl.py:4-5 is_allowed returns a bool that views.py:25 tests, but nothing normalizes the missing-ID case. acl.py:8-10 ensure_allowed aborts 403 only after views.py:16 has already dereferenced STORE[fid]. No handler in views.py converts KeyError to 404.
verdict.reason: The trace holds: STORE[fid] at views.py:16 and views.py:24 raises KeyError (500) for unknown IDs, while existing files reach ensure_allowed (views.py:17) or the 403 at views.py:26 / acl.py:10 for unauthorized callers, so any client that can call these routes can distinguish existing from missing IDs. Severity is low and depends on ID guessability, which the repo does not show.
